lines: ...A lantern. Nobody has carried a lantern through these halls in a hundred years.
Forgive me. I'm Pell. I kept the night door here, back when there were nights worth keeping.
You've come about the dark, haven't you? Everyone who comes, comes about the dark.
Still here, lantern-bearer? Good. The dark doesn't like being looked at.
One night every lamp went out at once. Every street, every window, every hearth-jet.
By morning the people were gone. I stayed. Porters stay.
I never learned why. The answer is still in this building, I think, if someone could put the pieces in order.
Ilsa Varn kept the valve watch. Quiet. Careful. Checked every gauge twice.
The night before, she asked me if I thought the Council could be trusted. I didn't answer her. I've had a long time to wish I had.
Ilsa always left a letter on the reception desk for the morning shift. The last one is still there. I never could bring myself to read it.
The guild children drew on the foyer wall while their parents worked the watch. One of them was awake that night. Look at what she drew.
Every watch was written in the logbook in the Watch Office, through the door at the end of the hall. Every watch, until the last one.
You've gathered what there is to gather. Now open your Chronicle and set it down: who, what, and when.
Mind you, the truth only holds if all three are true together. Half a truth is just another story.
So now you know. Ilsa closed the valve. Through the stone arch, down the stairs, the great wheel is waiting.
She left the numbers to reopen it. You've seen them.
Can you hear it? The pipes are singing. I'd forgotten that sound.
The lamps... You did it. Light in the halls. Light in the streets.
Whatever Ilsa was hiding the city from, it's had a hundred years to leave. Perhaps it's safe now.
Go on, lantern-bearer. There's a whole city waiting to be remembered.
Mind the dark. It minds you.
Shh. You'll wake the ledgers.
I'm Wren. I'm not supposed to be up here. Mama works the watch.
...Worked. Worked the watch. It's hard to remember which words go with now.
You came back. Nobody comes back.

choices.text: Did you make the chalk drawing?

lines: I saw the valve lady. She had her lantern, and she was crying, and she climbed right up onto the big wheel.
She turned it all the way round. Then everything went black at once, like closing your eyes.
That's mine! The valve lady making the night. I drew it so I wouldn't forget.
There were numbers too, underneath. A grown-up wrote them. I rubbed some out by accident. Don't tell.
Mama keeps the beacon. Kept. Orren says she's the best beacon-keeper there ever was.
Orren is nice. He gave me the chalk.
Will you come back when it's light?
The lamps! Look, look, the whole city!
Do you think Mama can see them, wherever she went?
